text:
isabel: FYI ran an afternoon stress run for EU pinned tenants. at 95th percentile load our eu pool hit hard capacity and ~22% of requests were routed to other regions. this exposed gaps in how we treat residency-sensitive traffic during transient saturation. want to agree a minimal outbound policy.
raf: do we have an operatorable SLA for enforced-residency tenants? blocking them is bad but we also shouldn't leak PII.
noor: legal already flagged two classes: strict (never leave region) and consentable (can leave if user/client explicitly opts in). we need deterministic behaviour per-tenant.
diego: suggestion: three-tier model: 
- strict: reject with 451 (Unavailable for Legal Reasons) when local capacity exhausted (and page oncall).
- consentable: serve local fallback and surface consent UI for higher-quality cross-region run, or honor a pre-sent consent header to avoid round-trip.
- best-effort: try local, then cross-region transparently if needed.
claire: I dislike using 451 for capacity because 451 signals legal prohibition. but I get the intent. maybe 503+ body explaining "residency-enforced" and operator escalation would be clearer. we could add `x-residency-block-code: strict` to make it searchable.
isabel: good point. alternate: 451 when tenant metadata says "legal_must_never_leave":true. otherwise 503 with `residency_reason`.
raf: how does consent flow look in practice? two RTTs will wreck UX for chat apps.
noor: we should support two flows: synchronous consent via header `X-Residency-Consent: id=consent123` where client pre-fetches user consent (with consent id issued via control plane) and asynchronous consent where fallback is returned immediately and an opt-in link is emitted in telemetry/console.
diego: implementation details: consent issuance endpoint: POST /v1/consents { tenant, scope, text } -> returns consent_id and consent_hash. store consent records in compliance DB (indexed by consent_hash) and mirror minimal audit to control-plane logs. responses should include `x-consent-id` for tracing.
claire: important: consent must be revocable. need to record both `consent_text` and `consent_locale` + timestamp. retention policies must be configurable per-customer. legal will provide defaults.
isabel: fallback model idea: tiny in-region distilled checkpoints (~150-250MB) served from CDN local edge. these should have strict runtime sandbox (no cross-region kv access) and mark outputs as lower-confidence. header `x-residency-outcome: fallback_local_v2` and `x-kv-availability: local_only`.
raf: session consistency: if user starts a conversation on strict tenant and falls back, we can't use cross-region KV. propose session tokens that encode last-kv-hash and are accepted by local caches. if later served cross-region (after consent) we reconcile at writeback. but reconcile complexity is high. maybe better to mark sessions immutable until reconciliation.
noor: agree. make fallback sessions append-only and flag `session_reconcile_required:true`. reconcile job must be operator-triggered or scheduled after consent.
diego: infra notes: prefer spinning up preemptible spot pool in-region for short bursts. if not available, preempt non-enforced tenants using a token-bucket preemption policy. also need a circuit-breaker that flips to "fallback-only" for a tenant after N failures within T window.
claire: telemetry: every request should carry `residency_decision:{requested,final,reason}` and we should emit metrics: residency_spill_rate, fallback_latency_p50/p95, consent_accepted_rate. console needs per-tenant drilldown and a stream of consent events.
isabel: API contract proposal (minimal): 
- Header `X-Residency-Requirement: strict|consentable|prefer_local|none`
- Header `X-Residency-Consent: consent_id=<id>` (optional)
- If strict + no capacity -> 451 with body {code: "RESIDENCY_ENFORCED"} and `x-residency-block-code: strict`
- If consentable + no capacity and no consent header -> 200 with degraded result (fallback) and `x-residency-outcome: fallback_local` plus `x-consent-link` in response metadata for async opt-in.
- If consentable + consent header present but consent invalid -> 428 Precondition Required with `x-residency-error: consent_invalid`
- Successful cross-region run must include `x-residency-evidence: consent_hash`

raf: 428 for invalid consent seems reasonable. we should standardize a small SDK helper that retries with the consent header when receiving 428.
noor: storage: store consent records in a compliance DB (encrypted at rest) and keep a hashed mirror in control-plane logs for traceability. also emit a compact consent-audit-event to our long-term audit store.
diego: build tasks for POC: 1) header parsing + quick path for pre-supplied consent id 2) small fallback artifact pipeline + CDN edge publication 3) residency telemetry fields 4) operator runbook for strict tenant starvation (auto-page, runbook steps) 5) SDK helper for consent handshake.
claire: I'd add a privacy-preserving consent hash algorithm (salted HMAC) so we can store proofs without leaking consent text. legal to sign off.
isabel: Infra-bot: stress report uploaded https://perf.redwood/sims/1749997777  shows 22% spill, fallback p50 160ms, cross-region p50 290ms, reconcile jobs avg 2.3s.
raf: timeline: can we aim for RFC + small POC (header + telemetry + fallback edge artifact) in 10 business days?
diego: yes for POC core work. reconciliation and audit retention follow after.
noor: legal will provide consent wording templates and retention guidelines by next Tue.
claire: I'll draft telemetry spec and consent-hash proposal.
isabel: thanks everyone. tagging @diego and @raf to lead POC. we'll reconvene after RFC draft.
infra-bot: action_created: RFC/residency-outbound-policy assigned to raf, due 10d
